data.name: Alexandrina
data.gender_notes: Alexandrina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Alexandros, meaning 'defender of the people'. In Greek mythology, Alexander the Great was known for his military prowess and conquest of the known world. The name Alexandrina carries the meaning “Defender of mankind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alexandrina usually hope their child will grow to embody defender of mankind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Alexandrina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defender of mankind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alexandrina total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Alexandrina is a namesake of Alexandros, a powerful name in Greek mythology and history. The cultural impact of this name is linked to its origin as a symbol of leadership, bravery, and strength. Throughout the centuries, this name has been associated with courageous rulers, inspiring military leaders, and renowned conquerors.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, Alexandrina is a reminder of how God offers protection and guidance to His people. Like Alexander the Great, we are all called to be defenders and champions of the faith in our own lives and communities. The name Alexandrina encourages us to trust in God's strength and power, and to live our lives as expressions of His love and compassion towards others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Alexandrina: Divine protector and illuminator of women. Embracing the strength and wisdom of Saint Alexander, Alexandrina denotes the feminine embodiment of divine guidance and courage.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
